findings.reason: the node is explicitly free to choose either option, and the one the text spells out in most detail is the one its own gate fails.
findings.text: the Deliverable says "A reservation is freed only when no process of its launch is alive … Age alone never frees it", and its negative control says "freeing it by age fails the fourth", yet three sentences later it offers "It may extend the attempt claim to the dispatch path, numbering the claim from the attempt being launched and freeing it by age … but it must meet both constraints named above" — the offered option violates the constraint the same paragraph names, so an implementer who takes the first option builds the exact behaviour the section's own case 4 is written to redden

findings.reason: a node that builds from its invocation and then checks the section would either build age-freed reservations and redden case 4, or stop to ask; the earlier followup defect in this same field (write paths) was raised and acted on for the same reason.
findings.text: the open followup that invokes §13 (`f-arolw-013`) still reads "takes a reservation that one of two racing doors holds and that frees itself by age", the pre-change behaviour, so the one hand-off a build node reads before the section states the opposite of the section's new freeing rule

findings.reason: a node told to show five cases has to drop one of six, and the dropped one may be the receipts case whose control is now misnumbered, so the gate can pass with the newest-receipt rule unmeasured.
findings.text: the Done-when still says "The new test then shows five cases" while the list beneath it now carries six bullets (the change added the launcher-alive case without updating the count), and the controls index cases by position so that "reading the lowest receipt instead of the newest fails the fifth" now points at the two-door race while the receipts case it describes is the sixth

findings.reason: an implementation that checks only the launcher passes all six cases and frees the reservation the moment the launcher dies, which reopens the worker.json gap this section exists to close.
findings.text: the freeing rule requires reading "the supervisor that launcher started" with its start tick, but the reservation is taken "before `_create_worktree`", long before `_start_supervisor` returns the supervisor pid (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2588), and the supervisor spec written before spawn carries no pid, so nothing in the stated sequence records the supervisor durably; the case list covers only "launcher dead and no supervisor alive" (case 3) and "launcher alive" (case 4), leaving the distinguishing case — launcher dead while its supervisor is still starting up — untested

response_events.note: §13's option text no longer offers freeing by age; it frees by the liveness of the launch's processes, matching the rule beside it.
f-arolw-013 now describes a reservation freed when no process of its launch is alive.
